notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 45-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.76, creatinine 0.89-0.91, hemoglobin 11.8-13.4, platelets 209-217, sodium 139-140, wbc 8.6-8.9; vitals dbp 72-77, heart_rate 77-82, map 91-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 128-133, spo2 96-98, temp 36.7-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.88-0.91, hemoglobin 10.5-11.5, platelets 207-216, sodium 139-140, wbc 8.3-8.5; vitals dbp 73-76, heart_rate 77-83, map 91-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 128-132, spo2 96-97, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 45-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
